learningJourney.title: What are Star Schemas, Fact Grain & Dimensions
learningJourney.explanation:
**Dimensional modeling** (Kimball) structures analytical warehouses around business processes rather than OLTP 3NF normalization. Numerical measurements sit in long, narrow **Fact tables** at a single declared **grain** (e.g., 1 row per checkout line item), surrounded by wide, denormalized **Dimension tables** (`dim_product`, `dim_customer`, `dim_date`) linked via deterministic **surrogate keys**.

Fact tables come in three types: **Transaction** (fully additive events), **Periodic Snapshot** (semi-additive daily balances), and **Accumulating Snapshot** (workflow milestones like `ordered_at -> shipped_at -> delivered_at`).
learningJourney.purpose: The mechanism: understand how Star Schemas, Fact Grain & Dimensions works from first principles.

learningJourney.title: Why 3NF Fails Analytics (and How Star Schemas + SCD2 Prevent Double-Counting)
learningJourney.explanation: Querying normalized 3NF tables directly forces 8-way joins, causes silent fan-out double-counting when joining headers to line items, and breaks historical attribution when a customer changes loyalty tier. **Star Schemas** need only 1-hop joins, and **SCD Type 2** (`valid_from`, `valid_to`, `is_current`) locks in the customer's tier *at purchase time*.

sectionDiagram.title: 1-Hop Star Join: fct_order_items -> Conformed Dimensions
sectionDiagram.summary: Denormalizing hierarchies into flat dimensions keeps BI queries to fast 1-hop joins while SCD Type 2 preserves point-in-time history.

ideas.title: E-Commerce Star Schema in BigQuery + dbt
ideas.description: Replacing 14 normalized MySQL tables with `fct_order_items` (line-item grain) + `dim_product` + `dim_customer` (SCD2) + `dim_date` cut Looker p95 from 18s to 1.4s and eliminated fan-out revenue bugs.

ideas.title: Accumulating Snapshot for Fulfillment SLAs
ideas.description: `fct_order_fulfillment` (1 row/order) tracks `ordered_at`, `packed_at`, `shipped_at`, and `delivered_at` via incremental dbt `merge`, making SLA lag queries trivial.

costs: Denormalized dimensions are expensive to update in-place on OLTP primaries.

learningJourney.title: How to manage Grain, Semi-Additive Measures & Late Dimensions
learningJourney.explanation:
1. **Never Mix Grains**: Don't put order-level `shipping_cost` on line-item rows without allocating it proportionally.
2. **Handle Orphan Facts**: Map unresolved late-arriving dimension keys to a `-1` ('Unknown') surrogate row and use `LEFT JOIN` in BI layers.
3. **Tag Semi-Additive Balances**: Never `SUM(account_balance)` across days—use `LAST_VALUE` over time and `SUM` across accounts.
4. **Partition by Date**: Partition large facts by `date_key` and cluster/Z-order by `product_sk` or `tenant_id`.
learningJourney.markdownContent:
```sql
-- Point-in-time SCD Type 2 join locking customer loyalty tier at purchase time
SELECT
    d.fiscal_quarter,
    c.loyalty_tier AS tier_at_purchase,
    SUM(f.net_revenue_cents) / 100.0 AS net_revenue
FROM fct_order_items f
JOIN dim_date d ON f.date_key = d.date_key
LEFT JOIN dim_customer_scd2 c
    ON f.customer_id = c.customer_id
   AND f.order_ts >= c.valid_from
   AND f.order_ts < COALESCE(c.valid_to, TIMESTAMP '9999-12-31 00:00:00')
GROUP BY 1, 2;
```

learningJourney.title: Alternatives: Star Schema vs. Snowflake vs. One Big Table (OBT) & SCD Types
learningJourney.explanation: Compare schema shapes and SCD strategies on storage cost, join speed, and backfill pain.

benefits: 1-hop joins; columnar Parquet dictionary/RLE encoding makes repeated strings nearly free.
Zero runtime joins—fastest for some flat BI extracts.
costs: Updating one customer attribute forces rewriting billions of historical fact rows.

comparison.choice: SCD Type 1 (Overwrite) vs. SCD Type 2 (Versioned Rows)
benefits: Type 1 is simple (1 row/entity) for typo fixes; Type 2 preserves full as-was history.
costs: Type 2 requires `is_current` or `[valid_from, valid_to)` range joins and overlap tests.

learningJourney.purpose: The trade-off: compare competing approaches across latency, consistency, and operational cost.

learningJourney.title: Production Architecture: SCD Type 2 Versioning & dbt Incremental Marts
learningJourney.explanation: In **dbt** + Parquet/Iceberg, model `stg_ -> int_ -> fct_/dim_`, generate deterministic MD5/SHA256 surrogate keys, materialize large facts as `incremental` (`merge` / `insert_overwrite` on `date_key`), and assert zero overlapping SCD2 `[valid_from, valid_to)` windows in CI.

sectionDiagram.title: Slowly Changing Dimension Type 2 Row Versioning
sectionDiagram.summary: Closing old rows with valid_to = change_ts and inserting a new current row preserves exact point-in-time attribution.

knowledgeCheck.question: An analyst runs `SELECT SUM(account_balance) FROM fct_daily_account_balances WHERE date BETWEEN '2026-11-01' AND '2026-11-30'` and reports 30x inflated customer balances. What modeling rule was violated?

options.text: `account_balance` in a Periodic Snapshot fact table is semi-additive—it can be summed across accounts on a single day, but never summed across days (use `LAST_VALUE` or `AVG` over time)
options.feedback: Correct: Periodic Snapshot balances are semi-additive and must not be summed across time.

options.text: The table should have been modeled as a Snowflake schema instead of a Star schema
options.feedback: Star vs Snowflake normalization does not change metric additivity.

options.text: Using surrogate keys instead of natural keys caused 30x fan-out
options.feedback: Surrogate keys prevent fan-out; the error here is summing a point-in-time balance across 30 daily snapshots.

_recommendedProblem.title: Active-Active Multi-Master Split-Brain Recovery
_recommendedProblem.prompt: Redesign an active-active multi-master relational replication pipeline between us-east-1 and eu-west-1 (6,000 writes/sec, 85 ms WAN RTT, < 15 ms p99 local commit) so a 9-minute transatlantic partition and 180-250 ms NTP clock skew never cause silent Last-Write-Wins (LWW) overwrites.
